source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: With I2C interboard cables limited to ≤30cm, the setup should work at 800kHz using the existing 4.4kΩ pull-ups.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Before you begin, here is V7. The I2C pull-ups were removed from this board because they have been moved to the main board, and that is the revision’s only change.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: To clarify my previous instruction, the resistors must not be removed.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text: The suitability and placement of the series resistors on the I2C bus are still unclear to me.

ambiguity.description: The suitability and placement of the I2C series resistors require client clarification.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Either option is acceptable: remove the 44Ω resistors if they complicate the layout, or leave them in place if they are already fitted and not obstructing anything.

Those resistors on SDA/SCL are only there for signal quality. Because I2C lines are open-drain, releasing them requires the pull-up resistor to recharge the cable capacitance to 3.3V. That can produce slight overshoot or ringing at the transition edge, which the series resistance damps.

With our 20–40cm cables and 4.4kΩ pull-ups, rise time will remain well within specification, so this should not be a meaningful problem.

main_board_i2c_series_resistors.installation_policy: optional; may be removed if they complicate layout or retained if already fitted without obstruction
